summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with weakness and confusion due to malignant hypercalcemia in the setting of relapsed refractory multiple myeloma. He had recently received pamidronate, so he was treated with IV fluids and nasal calcitonin instead. His hospital course was complicated by steroid-induced hyperglycemia requiring an insulin drip and subsequent insulin regimen adjustment, with glargine increased to 35 units nightly. His renal function fluctuated but stabilized with careful fluid management. He reported dyspnea on exertion, but imaging and V/Q scan ruled out pulmonary embolism or significant fluid overload; a pharmacologic stress test was arranged outpatient to evaluate for cardiac causes. He remained on oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis and continued chemotherapy with bortezomib and dexamethasone. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to monitor blood glucose four times daily, follow up with endocrinology and oncology, and schedule a cardiac stress test.
